region: Khovsgol ice, the Gobi and the central steppe
title: Mongolia — Ice, Camels and Gers at -25 C
subtitle: Winter on the Mongolian steppe: a frozen lake festival, Gobi dunes and herder-family nights
summary: Thirteen winter days that combine Lake Khovsgol's Ice Festival, the southern Gobi dunes and the Przewalski's horses at Hustai, hosted by herder families. Cold, remote and operator-dependent; the cost, fuel supply and festival dates are the main uncertainties.
introduction: Mongolia in early March is cold enough that the largest lake in the north is a road. At Khatgal the Ice Festival turns Lake Khovsgol into an arena for horse-sleighs, ice wrestling and shamanic rites; south in the Gobi, Bactrian camels stand in front of snow-dusted dunes at Khongoryn Els, and the gorge at Yolyn Am is a frozen walkway. Between them are two hundred kilometres of tracks that no sensible visitor drives alone in winter, so a driver-guide in a Russian-built van does the navigating, and the nights are in heated family gers. It is the group's coldest trip, and the one most dependent on local hosts.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman was a self-drive in dry heat with tents; this is -20 to -30 C, no self-drive, no tents, and a hosted stay in family gers where the cold itself is the destination.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: Package Mongolia is a July Gobi circuit with summer ger camps. Winter strips the crowds and the camps: the people who host you are herder families, not a tourism business.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: No other destination offers a festival on a frozen lake plus a desert in one week, and none is as dependent on the cold itself. The Caucasus and Norway are the nearest winter comparisons, but neither includes camels or ger stays.

duration.note: Day 1 outbound and day 13 return; the outbound flight lands early on day 2.

recommendedTravelWindow.window: 1-13 March 2027, shiftable by up to 5 days to match the announced Ice Festival dates
recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: The Khovsgol Ice Festival is held in early March (2-3 March in 2026) and March is 8-10 C warmer than February, which makes ger nights and the dunes more comfortable. Tsagaan Sar (7-9 Feb 2027) lies in the February window but then the festival is missed.

februarySuitability.summary: Coldest month (Ulaanbaatar day highs about -10 C, nights about -24 C; Khatgal colder). Tsagaan Sar (7-9 Feb) is a cultural highlight, but many shops and some operators close for several days and the Ice Festival falls after it.

marchSuitability.summary: Still winter but with longer days and milder afternoons (Ulaanbaatar highs about 0 C, Dalanzadgad about 4 C). Ice at Khovsgol is thickest and the festival runs in early March (official 2027 dates not yet announced).

february.rainfall: Almost no precipitation; Gobi and Ulaanbaatar are dry and sunny with occasional snow.
february.notes: Wind chill and blizzards are the main hazard.

march.rainfall: Little precipitation; snowfall possible in March.

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: Roads are mostly unpaved tracks; snow drifts and blizzards can close sections. Flights can be cancelled by wind or fog. Lake Khovsgol ice is usually over 1 m thick by March.
climate.seaConditions: Not relevant: no sea. Lake ice is safe only with local drivers who know thickness and currents.
climate.airQuality: Ulaanbaatar winter smog from ger-district coal and vehicles is among the world's worst from December to February (S16); March is better but not clean. Rural areas are clear.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Bactrian camels, ibex and wolves are visible in the Gobi; takhi at Hustai; reindeer are far north and not on this route.

geography.summary: A route from a frozen lake in the Sayan taiga to the Gobi dunes, crossing steppe at 1,100-1,700 m.
geography.distinctive: Lake Khovsgol holds about 70% of Mongolia's fresh water and freezes thick enough to drive on; the Gobi dunes of Khongoryn Els sit against a snow-dusted Altai range.

culture.summary: Pastoral nomadic life, Tibetan Buddhism, shamanism and the festival calendar, experienced through herder families.

culturalHighlights.name: Khovsgol Ice Festival
culturalHighlights.description: Locally organised winter festival with horse-sleigh racing, ice wrestling, shagai and shamanic rites; locals are hosts, so dates and customs should be confirmed with the operator.

culturalHighlights.description: Main working Buddhist monastery in Ulaanbaatar; visit during morning prayers.

culturalHighlights.name: Herder family gers (Khongor, Hustai, Terelj)
culturalHighlights.description: Nights with families who keep camels, horses or livestock; hospitality is by established custom (tea, gifts of tea or sweets) and arranged through the operator.

culturalHighlights.name: Winter food and Tsagaan Sar traditions
culturalHighlights.description: Frozen-meat butchering, buuz dumplings and dairy; Tsagaan Sar itself falls on 7-9 Feb, outside the March window.

adventureHighlights.name: Ice driving and horse-sleigh on Lake Khovsgol
adventureHighlights.description: Vehicle and sleigh excursions on the ice with local drivers only.

adventureHighlights.name: Khongoryn Els dune climb and camel ride
adventureHighlights.description: Short walk to the ridge at -15 C with wind chill; camel ride with a herder family.

adventureHighlights.name: Yolyn Am frozen gorge walk
adventureHighlights.description: 2-3 h walk on the valley ice; microspikes recommended.

adventureHighlights.name: Extreme-cold exposure management
adventureHighlights.description: -20 to -30 C days need layers, balaclavas and rest stops to prevent frostbite.

signatureExperiences.title: The Ice Festival on Lake Khovsgol
signatureExperiences.description: A two-day festival on the frozen lake at Khatgal with horse-sleigh racing, ice wrestling, shagai, ice skating and shamanic rituals, plus a horse-sleigh ride and a drive over the ice.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: One of the few winter festivals held on a frozen lake in the world, run by the local community.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Fly UB-Moron, then a driver-guide van to Khatgal. Book a family ger or guesthouse by January; confirm festival dates with the organiser before booking flights.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Activities estimate (horse-sleigh, ice drive, local events); festival entry generally free.

signatureExperiences.title: A night with a camel-herding family at Khongoryn Els
signatureExperiences.description: Stay in a heated family ger at the foot of the singing dunes, climb the ridge and ride a Bactrian camel across the frozen valley.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Winter removes the tourist camps; the only beds are in family gers, and the dunes carry snow.
signatureExperiences.location: Khongoryn Els, Gobi Gurvansaikhan National Park
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Fly UB-Dalanzadgad, then 4x4 via Bayanzag (about 5-6 h). The operator arranges the family; bring a -30 C sleeping bag.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Ger night 22, camel ride and park fees; excluding transport.

signatureExperiences.title: Frozen Yolyn Am and the Flaming Cliffs
signatureExperiences.description: Walk the ice-floored gorge at Yolyn Am, then stand on the rim of Bayanzag where dinosaur eggs were first found in the 1920s.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: A frozen Gobi gorge is unusual; in summer the gorge ice is gone.
signatureExperiences.location: Gobi Gurvansaikhan National Park and Bayanzag
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Day trip from Dalanzadgad with the driver-guide; microspikes for the valley floor.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Park and site entry only; transport and guide are in the shared budget.

signatureExperiences.title: Przewalski's horses in the snow at Hustai
signatureExperiences.description: A ranger-guided evening at Hustai National Park to see takhi herds, with a ger night near the reserve.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: The takhi are the only truly wild horse species and were reintroduced to Hustai from zoos.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Drive 2 h from Ulaanbaatar or fly into UB after the Gobi; park access is ranger-guided.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Park fee and ranger; ger night per person 22 is in accommodation.

travelStyle.summary: Licensed driver-guide in a 4x4 van, four internal flights and family-hosted ger nights; no self-drive.

transport.summary: Roads outside Ulaanbaatar are mostly unpaved tracks (only about 10% paved), signposting is minimal and winter blizzards are frequent, so a local driver with a Russian UAZ Furgon or a Hyundai Starex is essential. Domestic flights (Hunnu Air, Aero Mongolia, MIAT) save 20-24 h of winter driving but run on limited schedules and are weather-dependent.

modes.description: Operator vehicle with a local driver; average speeds 30-65 km/h.
UB-Moron and UB-Dalanzadgad; 15 kg baggage limit; not daily.
Overnight UB-Erdenet train is used by some operators (not used here), but is slow and offers no extra access.

transport.carRental: Self-drive rental is not recommended in winter: tracks are unmarked, there is no mobile coverage in large rural areas and fuel is intermittent. Operators provide vehicle plus driver (about USD 100-130 per day).

drivingRequirements.summary: Self-drive is not feasible: unmarked tracks, -30 C, no network in much of the country, fuel disruption and a 1968 IDP requirement.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: A 1968 Vienna Convention IDP is required by Mongolia (FCDO); 1949 IDPs are not accepted; the Netherlands also states an IDP is required.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four hold car licences, but they are not needed because a local driver drives the whole route.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: No motorcycle or scooter use. Alternatives: driver-guide van, horse-sleigh, camel ride, dog-sled, walking.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: Use a licensed operator's vehicle and driver. Avoid unlicensed taxis.

accommodation.summary: City and provincial hotels or guesthouses in Ulaanbaatar, Khatgal and Dalanzadgad, and heated family gers at Khongor, Hustai and Terelj. Winter tourist ger camps are mostly closed (15 May-15 Oct season), so these are homestays; toilets are outdoor and showers are in town bathhouses.

camping.summary: Tent camping at -20 to -30 C is not recommended; heated family gers are the winter norm.

physicalDifficulty.label: strenuous
physicalDifficulty.summary: Difficulty comes from cold, not distance: -20 to -30 C nights, long bumpy drives, simple toilets and limited medical access. Walks are short.

itinerary.summary: Ulaanbaatar, a flight to Khovsgol for the Ice Festival, back to the capital, a flight to the Gobi for Yolyn Am and Khongoryn Els, and a finish at Hustai and Terelj; two contingency days.

stops.name: Ulaanbaatar, Gandan Monastery
stops.description: Capital at 1,350 m with temperatures near -25 C at night in February. Gandan is the main working Buddhist monastery; winter air pollution from ger-district heating is highest from December to February.
stops.culturalImportance: Centre of Mongolian Buddhism, re-established after the 1990 restoration of religious freedom.
stops.geography: Tuul River valley between four sacred mountains.

stops.name: Moron (Moron airport)
stops.description: Capital of Khovsgol Province. Domestic flight about 1 h 15 min from Ulaanbaatar; the alternative is 10-12 h by road.

stops.name: Khatgal
stops.description: Village at the southern tip of Lake Khovsgol, base for the Ice Festival and for ice-driving and horse-sleigh rides. Heated gers and guesthouses fill early.
stops.culturalImportance: Locally run winter festival on the lake; shamanic and Buddhist traditions.
stops.geography: 1,650 m at the foot of the Sayan taiga.

stops.name: Lake Khovsgol (frozen, southern shore)
stops.description: Lake roughly 136 km long, ice usually over 1 m thick in March; vehicles drive on it. Coordinates are an approximate point on the southern ice near Khatgal.
activities: Walking and vehicle excursions on the ice (with local driver)
stops.geography: Alpine rift lake in the Sayan foothills, one of Asia's largest freshwater reserves.
stops.transport: UAZ van on ice with local driver only

stops.name: Dalanzadgad
stops.description: Provincial centre of Omnogovi and gateway to the southern Gobi; domestic flight from Ulaanbaatar about 1 h 15 min.

stops.name: Yolyn Am
stops.description: Narrow gorge in the Gobi Altai where ice remains on the valley floor into early summer; in February-March a frozen walk of 2-3 h.
activities: Walk along the frozen valley floor
stops.geography: Granite-limestone gorge in Gobi Gurvansaikhan National Park.

stops.name: Bayanzag (Flaming Cliffs)
stops.description: Red sandstone cliffs where Roy Chapman Andrews's 1920s expeditions found the first dinosaur eggs; winter sun makes them glow.
stops.geography: Basin with saxaul scrub at about 1,500 m.

stops.name: Khongoryn Els (singing dunes) herder family ger
stops.description: Dunes up to about 300 m high and 100+ km long on the north side of the Gobi Gurvansaikhan range; Bactrian camel herding families live along the Khongor river. Coordinates are an approximate centre (to verify).
activities: Night in a heated family ger

stops.geography: Sand sea against the snow-dusted Altai range.
stops.transport: Van, about 3 h from Bayanzag; about 4-5 h back to Dalanzadgad in winter

stops.name: Hustai National Park (Khustain Nuruu)
stops.description: Steppe reserve where Przewalski's horses (takhi) were reintroduced; about 100 km west of Ulaanbaatar.

security.summary: No official advice recommends against travel to the route regions, and the Netherlands rates Mongolia yellow. The status is conditional because of an unresolved fuel-supply crisis that two authorities flag as able to disrupt flights, road travel and remote access, an expiring Dutch advisory, and winter-extreme conditions with limited rural medical care.
security.assessedRoute: Ulaanbaatar, Khovsgol (Moron, Khatgal, lake), southern Gobi (Dalanzadgad, Yolyn Am, Bayanzag, Khongoryn Els), Hustai and Terelj; Bayan-Olgii in the far west is deliberately not included.

advisories.level: No 'against all travel' or 'all but essential travel' warning; warning about fuel shortages including aviation fuel (page updated 7 Aug 2026, still current 28 Nov 2026)
advisories.routeImpact: Possible disruption to domestic flights, road travel and remote areas; reassess before booking.

advisories.level: No country-wide formal warning found; notices on bear attack near Ulaanbaatar (8 Oct 2026), foot-and-mouth outbreak in Bayan-Olgii (7 Aug 2026), fuel rationing (10 Sep 2026); page updated 14 Oct 2026. The security-zone colour was not readable on the fetched page.
advisories.routeImpact: Route avoids the west; avoid forest hikes near UB; fuel measures to be rechecked.

advisories.level: Yellow (specific risks); updated 28 Aug 2026, shown as valid until 28 Nov 2026 (renewal not yet seen)
advisories.regionsAffected: Border zones; Ulaanbaatar and trains for crime
advisories.routeImpact: Frontier-zone permit needed near Khovsgol; limited rural healthcare.

advisories.level: General global terrorism threat; extreme winter weather and high road accident rates
advisories.routeImpact: Covered by driver-guide approach and insurance.

conflictRisk.note: No armed conflict; occasional political protests in Ulaanbaatar.

terrorismRisk.note: No recent history of attacks (FCDO) despite the general global threat statement.

regionalRestrictions: Border zones up to 100 km inland need State Frontier Guard permission (Khovsgol is within it).
Foot-and-mouth restrictions in Bayan-Olgii (not on the route).
Photographing military and police is prohibited.
ordinaryRisks: Cold and frostbite at -20 to -30 C
Thin ice at river mouths on Lake Khovsgol
security.medicalAccess: Limited in rural areas; Netherlands advice says serious cases may need transfer to China, treatment may require upfront payment, and altitude sickness is possible in mountainous areas.
security.insuranceConsiderations: Insurance must cover winter conditions, remote evacuation and repatriation. Check exclusions for ice, off-piste and remote areas.
security.reassessmentRequired: Re-check FCDO, France and Netherlands advice before booking and two weeks before departure; trigger: fuel rationing renewed, flights cancelled for aviation-fuel shortage, a new FMD or other outbreak on the route, or the Netherlands advisory moving above yellow.

practicalRequirements.visa: Conditional on nationality. France and 33 other nationalities are visa-free for up to 30 days until 1 January 2027, with extension into 2027 unconfirmed (S06); the UK page says the same date (S05); the Netherlands page says 30 days visa-free (S04). If it lapses, an e-visa costs about USD 51.50 (S07). Check the Mongolian immigration agency or consulate.
practicalRequirements.entry: Carry the passport (copies not accepted by police); ask for an entry stamp; foreigners may need to register within a short period.
practicalRequirements.passportValidity: At least six months after arrival (UK) or after departure (Netherlands).
practicalRequirements.insurance: Mandatory in practice: winter cold, remote evacuation, repatriation.
practicalRequirements.connectivity: Local SIMs work in cities and towns; large rural areas have no network, so a satellite phone or operator radio is advisable.
practicalRequirements.payments: Mongolian tugrik; cards in Ulaanbaatar and Dalanzadgad, cash in rural areas.
practicalRequirements.medical: Hospitals in Ulaanbaatar only; bring medications in original packaging; altitude and measles vaccination status check.
practicalRequirements.fuel: Fuel supply was disrupted in autumn 2026; reconfirm before booking.

advantages: Unique winter combination: frozen-lake festival plus Gobi dunes and wild horses.
Very few tourists, so everything runs through family hosts.
Dry cold is easier to tolerate than damp cold, and skies are clear.
Strong cultural content: herder families, Tibetan Buddhism, shamanism.
disadvantages: Extreme cold with frostbite risk and simple toilets.
Needs four domestic flights and an operator; no self-drive.
Total cost is likely above the group's EUR 2,500 limit.
Ice Festival dates are not yet confirmed.
uncertainties: Fuel supply: FCDO and France flag shortages and rationing; the situation was improving in November (reserves 12 days of petrol, 28 days of diesel, 36 days of aviation fuel) but is unresolved.
Ice Festival 2027 dates are not announced; the itinerary must be shifted to match.
Visa-free regime ends 1 January 2027 on the sources found; extension into March 2027 is unconfirmed.
Winter domestic flight schedules and fares were not verified.
An eagle festival in March in Bayan-Olgii could not be verified, so it is excluded (main festival is in autumn).
